title: Holiness and Preparation for the Journey

date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative and legislation
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the holiness and preparation for the journey material across Numbers 5–10.
claims.evidence: Numbers 5–10; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: The exact archaeological or external historical setting of this entire passage has not been independently established.
claims.evidence: Phase 1/2: no independent archaeological or external historical identification of the Num 5-10 wilderness setting; Phase 2 records the literary relationship of Num 5-10 to priestly Torah formation as Debated (Frevel) and limits Ketef Hinnom to late-preexilic circulation of related blessing language, not the date of Numbers as a book. QA Phase 4 §5.2: Ketef Hinnom now supported by Waaler 2002 (verified, read in full); Barkay 2004 full article unread (abstract/metadata only); KJV chs. 6-10 still not independently verified.

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

connections.note: Restitution half (Lev 5:5-13: confession and repayment with a fifth part) plus guilt-offering material (Lev 5:14-6:7) provides the legal counterpart to Numbers 5:5-10.
Related Nazirite consecration tradition with important differences.
Primary Passover legislation, supplemented in Numbers 9.
Only other explicit Old Testament Nazirite mention: Amos says YHWH raised up Nazarites and Israel gave them wine; prophetic indictment, not a restatement of the Numbers 6 vow law.
Blessing echo of Numbers 6:24-26 ('cause his face to shine upon us'); liturgical parallel, not a quotation.
Later vow practice: Paul joins four men under a vow, purifies himself with them and pays for their head-shaving; continuity of vow custom, not a retelling of Numbers 6.

Tabernacle erected and dedicated (the setting for the offerings of Numbers 7) and the cloud covering the tent with the glory filling the tabernacle (Exod 40:34-38), the guidance that opens Numbers 9:15-23.
Hezekiah's Passover kept in the second month for those unclean or absent: the later analogue of the postponed Passover provision in Numbers 9:1-14.
Levite census, clans and duties grounding the consecration of the Levites in Numbers 8; also the context for the age discrepancy (service from age 30 here, age 25 in Numbers 8:24-26).
Pattern for the gold lampstand, made 'after the pattern' shown on the mountain; the lampstand Numbers 8:1-4 lights.
'Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered' echoes the ark saying of Numbers 10:35 ('Rise up, LORD'); later liturgical reception, not a narrative parallel.

Marital and sexual-accusation law (including a husband's charge against his wife) offering the closest legal parallel to the suspected-adultery ordeal of Numbers 5:11-31, with a different procedure: judicial penalties, no ordeal.
